newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Adidas sprints to higher Q3 profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Adidas sprints to higher Q3 profits.

text.p: Adidas AG on Tuesday sprinted to higher nine-month profits as the German sportswear maker reported 44 percent growth in North American sales and began preparing for its lucrative the 1998 soccer World Cup sponsorship deal.
Adidas said it expected "further steady growth" after third-quarter net income rose 17 percent to 150 million marks ($100.4 million) while sales rose 35 percent to 1.47 billion marks.
On a nine-month basis, adidas said net income rose 29 percent to 324 million marks while sales surged 31 percent to 3.71 billion marks.
"Our business outlook, based on a 30 percent increase in our order backlog, is very positive," adidas chief executive Robert Louis-Dreyfus said in a statement.
"We are expecting further steady growth for adidas."
Shares in adidas rose on the results, climbing 1.50 marks to 134.00 marks and outpacing the broader 30-share DAX index.
Adidas said about 500,000 pairs of its new "Feet You Wear" shoes launched in the third quarter had been sold by the end of September.
Adidas, best known for its three-stripe logo, also said it was preparing to launch products for Christmas linked to its sponsorship status with the 1998 World Cup.

Adidas in October announced it had bought the rights to be an official sponsor of the event, whose championship will be played in France, and also acquired global licensing rights for the event, the first time a sportswear maker has done so.

The latest results confirmed the recovery at Adidas led by Louis-Dreyfus, a former top executive at British advertising group Saatchi & Saatchi, after he gained control of the legendary Herzogenaurach-based group in late 1992.
As part of the recovery, Adidas said its apparel sales surged some 45.5 percent during the third quarter while overall footwear sales rose 24.2 percent over year-ago levels.
Europe was still the engine behind the brand's growth, with sales topping one billion marks for the first time in company history to 1.01 billion marks.
Sales in North America grew by an above-average 44 percent to 314 million marks from 218 million marks in the 1995 third quarter, adidas said in a statement.

Net sales in the Asia-Pacific region grew to 119 million marks from 98 million marks, a year-on-year gain of 22 percent, while turnover in Latin America rose 17 percent to 28 million marks from 24 million marks.

For the first nine months of the year, Adidas said European sales rose to 2.53 billion marks from 1.91 billion marks in the year-ago period, while sales in North America rose by 27 percent and in Asia by 30 percent.
Adidas said its trade receivables rose 36 percent to 953 million marks as of September 30, which was slightly above the sales growth of 35 percent for the third quarter.
The company said almost one-third of the growth was due to the inclusion of an Italian joint venture on 1996 results.

Inventories rose by 36.2 percent to 828 million marks. "The major reasons behind this increase are an increase in open orders and, to a lesser extent, the inclusion of new subsidiaries," adidas said in a statement.
Order backlog remained strong, with the level as of September 30 for deliveries scheduled from October 1996 to March 1997 up 30 percent over year-ago levels.
